key_insight: HVOF WC-17Co coatings maintain the best wear performance at 200–400 °C, with a minimum around 400 °C due to protective tribo-oxide formation and compacted debris.
engineering_relevance: For high-temperature sliding components, WC-17Co HVOF coatings are promising up to about 400 °C, but performance degrades sharply at 500–600 °C from oxidation and binder damage.
method: HVOF-deposited WC-17Co coating tested in dry sliding wear from room temperature to 600 °C.
Characterized with SEM, EDS, XRD, and 3D surface profilometry before and after wear.
Measured coating thickness, porosity, roughness, wear-track morphology, and phase changes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ~268.99 μm coating thickness, 1.53% porosity, and 10.2 μm average roughness, with lowest wear/friction at 400 °C and a marked wear increase at 500–600 °C.
watch_item: The favorable temperature window is application-specific; above 400 °C, oxide-layer instability and Co-binder degradation may limit long-term durability.
paper_title: Effect of thermal exposure on the wear and phase stability of HVOF-deposited WC-17Co coatings
